definitions.rationale: This is the macro expansion defining the named loopBody AST term; it introduces syntax for the exact loop body and does not add an execution or mathematical fact.
definitions.text:
rule loopBody
    => Assign(
         Name("reversed_s"),
         BinOp("+", Name("c"), Name("reversed_s")))
       If(
         Call(Attribute(Name("c"), "isalpha"), .Exprs),
         AugAssign(
           Name("swapped"),
           "+",
           Call(Attribute(Name("c"), "swapcase"), .Exprs))
         Assign(Name("has_letter"), Bool(true))
         .Stmts,
         AugAssign(Name("swapped"), "+", Name("c"))
         .Stmts)
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This is the macro expansion defining the named solveBody AST term used by the claims; it is a syntactic definition of the exact program body.
definitions.text:
rule solveBody
    => Expr(
         Str("Toggle letter case, or reverse a string containing no letters."))
       Assign(Name("swapped"), Str(""))
       Assign(Name("reversed_s"), Str(""))
       Assign(Name("has_letter"), Bool(false))
       Assign(Name("c"), Str(""))
       For(Name("c"), Name("s"), loopBody)
       If(
         Name("has_letter"),
         Return(Name("swapped")) .Stmts,
         .Stmts)
       Return(Name("reversed_s"))
       .Stmts

definitions.rationale: This equation defines charAlpha for a one-character modeled string in terms of the existing nonemptiness test and allAlpha helper.
This is the base equation of the alphaAcc recurrence, returning the accumulated alphabetic-character flag when no input remains.
This simplification is the alphabetic recursive equation of the alphaAcc definition; under charAlpha(C) it advances structurally and sets the accumulator to true.
definitions.text:
rule alphaAcc(iCons(C:Int, REST:IntSeq), FOUND:Bool)
    => alphaAcc(REST, true)
    requires charAlpha(C)
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This simplification is the non-alphabetic recursive equation of the alphaAcc definition; under the complementary guard it advances structurally and preserves the accumulator.
definitions.text:
rule alphaAcc(iCons(C:Int, REST:IntSeq), FOUND:Bool)
    => alphaAcc(REST, FOUND)
    requires notBool charAlpha(C)
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This is the base equation of the toggleAcc recurrence, returning the accumulated output when no input remains.
This simplification is the alphabetic recursive equation defining toggleAcc; it appends swapC(C) to the output accumulator and recurses on REST.
definitions.text:
rule toggleAcc(iCons(C:Int, REST:IntSeq), OUT:IntSeq)
    => toggleAcc(
         REST,
         seqConcat(OUT, iCons(swapC(C), .IntSeq)))
    requires charAlpha(C)
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This simplification is the complementary non-alphabetic recursive equation defining toggleAcc; it appends C unchanged and recurses on REST.
definitions.text:
rule toggleAcc(iCons(C:Int, REST:IntSeq), OUT:IntSeq)
    => toggleAcc(
         REST,
         seqConcat(OUT, iCons(C, .IntSeq)))
    requires notBool charAlpha(C)
    [simplification]

definitions.rationale: This is the empty-input base equation defining lastChar as the supplied initial loop-target value.
This is the structural recursive equation defining lastChar by retaining the current character and continuing through REST.
This guarded equation defines the alphabetic-input branch of solveResult using the toggleAcc summary.
definitions.text:
rule solveResult(INPUT:IntSeq) => str(toggleAcc(INPUT, .IntSeq))
    requires alphaAcc(INPUT, false)

definitions.rationale: This complementary guarded equation defines the no-alphabetic-character branch of solveResult using revIS.
definitions.text:
rule solveResult(INPUT:IntSeq) => str(revIS(INPUT))
    requires notBool alphaAcc(INPUT, false)

source_rules.rationale: This simplification adds the constructor-disjointness fact that a one-element IntSeq is not empty. Stage 1 proves the same fact in the lemma-only definition, but prove.sh compiles and uses this rule in the main proof before running that separate proof, so it does not satisfy the required first-proved ordering for PROVED_DERIVED_LEMMA.
